title: Bone Loss & Resistive Countermeasure Protocol
trigger_patterns: ARED mechanical resistive training volume falls below minimum protective threshold (< 8,000 kg*reps/day)
Urinary calcium excretion biomarker indicates elevated osteoclastic bone resorption
Long-duration mission phase (Mission Day > 60) musculoskeletal deconditioning alert

steps.text: Review weekly ARED (Advanced Resistive Exercise Device) telemetry: audit cumulative mechanical load, peak eccentric ground reaction forces, and session completion rate.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: If a deficit is detected, schedule targeted compensatory resistive sessions prioritizing axial loading exercises (deadlifts, squats, heel raises with maximum tolerable load bar settings).
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Perform point-of-care urinary biomarker strip test for urinary calcium concentration to detect active bone mineral leaching.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: If urinary calcium is elevated (> 7.5 mmol/L), increase daily hydration target to at least 2.8 L/day to prevent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis (spaceflight kidney stone formation).
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Audit daily nutritional logs: confirm 800-1000 IU Vitamin D3 supplementation and balanced calcium intake without excessive protein-induced hypercalciuria.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Document musculoskeletal countermeasure adherence and transmit weekly structural integrity log to ground biomechanics team.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure
